reference.title: Kettlebell Alternating Renegade Row
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be read at authoring time because the proxy blocked it, so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Exhale on each row, inhale as you lower; keep a steady brace in between.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up, 0.3 s squeeze, 1 s down per side

prescription.tempo: 1-0-1 per side, short pause between sides
prescription.load: User-chosen kettlebells, light to moderate; stop about 2 reps short of failure or when the hips start to twist
prescription.progression: Narrow the feet, then add load

cues.text: High plank with each hand gripping a kettlebell under the shoulder, feet wider than the hips, body in one line.
Push the other kettlebell into the floor and row one kettlebell to the hip, elbow close.
Hips stay level and square to the floor.
Set the kettlebell down quietly under the shoulder.
Re-brace in the plank, then row the other side.

mistakes.mistake: Hips twisting open toward the rowing side
mistakes.fix: Widen the feet, squeeze the glutes and use lighter kettlebells.
Hold one straight line from head to heels.

mistakes.mistake: Kettlebells too far apart or tipping
mistakes.fix: Set them right under the shoulders on a flat, non-slip floor; press straight down through the handle.

kinematics.norm: Straight line from head to heels, hips level (clinical opinion)
From straight to about 90 degrees, the kettlebell at the lower ribs (clinical opinion)
Feet wider than the hips for a stable base (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1 s up and 1 s down per side (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual 13773, Kettlebell Alternating Renegade Row, video (movement reference)
Fenwick, Brown & McGill 2009, comparison of different rowing exercises: trunk muscle activation and lumbar spine motion, load and stiffness (J Strength Cond Res 23(2):350-358)
Lehman et al. 2004, variations in muscle activation levels during traditional latissimus dorsi weight training exercises (Dynamic Medicine 3:4)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
The kettlebell load is your choice: pick a weight you can move with the form shown for every rep.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Wrist pain: keep the wrists straight over the handles.
Kettlebells can tip under a plank: press straight down through the handle and use bells with flat, wide bases.
modify: Hard to keep the hips still: do it from the knees or widen the feet.
regressions: One-arm kettlebell row on a bench.

muscleNotes.lats_r: Main shoulder extensor: pulls the elbow from below the shoulder back beside the trunk.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Main shoulder extensor: pulls the elbow from below the shoulder back beside the trunk.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Squeeze the shoulder blade back at the top; rows gave the highest middle trapezius/rhomboid activity of the pulls tested by Lehman 2004.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Squeeze the shoulder blade back at the top; rows gave the highest middle trapezius/rhomboid activity of the pulls tested by Lehman 2004.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Helps extend the shoulder as the elbow passes the trunk.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Helps extend the shoulder as the elbow passes the trunk.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Flexes the elbow; the neutral grip shares the work with brachialis and brachioradialis.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Flexes the elbow; the neutral grip shares the work with brachialis and brachioradialis.
muscleNotes.core: Hold the plank and stop the hips sagging or twisting while one hand is off the floor (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist rotation toward the lifted side; a one-armed row challenged the torsional capacity of the trunk muscles (Fenwick 2009).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist rotation toward the lifted side; a one-armed row challenged the torsional capacity of the trunk muscles (Fenwick 2009).
muscleNotes.pec_r: The support arm holds the top of a push-up.
muscleNotes.pec_l: The support arm holds the top of a push-up.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Holds the support shoulder blade against the ribs.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Holds the support shoulder blade against the ribs.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Squeeze to keep the hips level with the shoulders.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Squeeze to keep the hips level with the shoulders.
muscleNotes.quads_r: Keep the knees straight in the plank.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Keep the knees straight in the plank.
